title: Crossmodal correspondences: A tutorial review
review_question: To review the existence, nature, and consequences of crossmodal correspondences for human information processing and multisensory integration, and their role in solving the crossmodal binding problem.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Primarily focuses on crossmodal correspondences between auditory and visual stimuli, while acknowledging and briefly mentioning associations across other sensory modalities.

findings.antecedent: Various unisensory features (e.g., auditory pitch, visual size, brightness, shape, elevation, loudness)
findings.quote: A large body of research now shows that people exhibit consistent crossmodal correspondences between many stimulus features

findings.antecedent: Crossmodally incongruent auditory and visual stimuli (e.g., high pitch with large visual object)
findings.consequent: Response time and accuracy in speeded classification tasks
findings.source: Assessing the impact of crossmodal correspondences on human information processing using the speeded classification task
findings.quote: Marks reported that people find it harder (i.e., they are slower and less accurate) to classify the target stimuli

findings.antecedent: Crossmodally congruent auditory and visual stimuli
findings.source: Do crossmodal correspondences influence multisensory integration/perception? Temporal integration
findings.quote: The results... demonstrated that Parise and Spence's (2009) participants found it significantly harder to correctly resolve the temporal order

findings.antecedent: Peculiarities of neural systems coding sensory information (e.g., magnitude representation, nearby brain areas)
findings.consequent: Structural crossmodal correspondences (e.g., loudness-brightness, pitch-elevation, pitch-size)
findings.quote: The first class of crossmodal correspondence result from the peculiarities of the neural systems we use to code sensory information.

findings.antecedent: Internalization of natural correlations between stimulus attributes in the environment (e.g., object size and resonant frequency)
findings.consequent: Statistical crossmodal correspondences (e.g., pitch-elevation, pitch-size, loudness-size, pitch-spatial frequency)
findings.quote: The second class of cross-modal correspondence for which there is robust support reflect an adaptive response by our brains to the regularities of the world

findings.antecedent: Common linguistic terms used to describe stimuli along different perceptual continua (e.g., 'high' and 'low' for pitch and elevation)
findings.consequent: Semantically mediated crossmodal correspondences (e.g., pitch-elevation, pitch-spatial frequency)
findings.quote: The third class of crossmodal correspondence result when common linguistic terms are used to describe the stimuli falling along different continua

findings.consequent: Strength of coupling priors in Bayesian integration models
findings.source: Explaining crossmodal correspondences in terms of Bayesian priors
findings.quote: the notion of crossmodal correspondences might be modelled within such a framework as a form of prior knowledge.

findings.antecedent: Repeated exposure to statistical co-occurrence of initially unrelated stimuli (training)
findings.consequent: Neural activity (e.g., enhanced crossmodal connectivity, altered preparatory neural activity)
findings.source: Assessing the neural substrates underlying crossmodal correspondences
findings.quote: The evidence emerging from the neuroimaging studies published to date therefore supports the view that the establishment of novel learned associations... results in enhanced crossmodal connectivity

synthesis_conclusions: Crossmodal correspondences modulate multisensory integration at both decisional and perceptual levels.

Crossmodal correspondences influence performance in a wide range of tasks, including direct crossmodal matching, speeded classification, simple detection, Implicit Association Test, unspeeded TOJs, spatial localization, and perceptual discrimination.
Crossmodal correspondences are established automatically and can affect late decisional processes as well as, under certain conditions, perceptual integration.
There are at least three distinct kinds of crossmodal correspondence: structural, statistical, and semantically mediated.
Crossmodal correspondences play an important role in constraining the crossmodal binding problem.
evidence_gaps: Unclear how to resolve discrepancies between significant perceptual effects and null results on perceptual sensitivity for different correspondences.
Need clearer distinction between different kinds of crossmodal correspondence (structural, statistical, semantic) and their underlying neural substrates/effects.
Unresolved question of the innateness of crossmodal correspondences.
Need more direct means of testing for natural regularities in the environment (e.g., recording audiovisual footage).
Need to investigate specific crossmodal correspondences using a variety of different experimental paradigms.
Need to investigate neural changes associated with learning novel crossmodal associations over longer time periods.
limitations: The relative contributions of perceptual and decisional factors to crossmodal interactions likely depend on the particular pairing of dimensions and the task.
The tripartite categorization (structural, statistical, semantic) is not exhaustive; other classes of crossmodal correspondence may exist (e.g., based on affective effects).

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Crossmodal correspondences arise from shared abstract properties or dimensions (e.g., magnitude, intensity, arousal) that are common across different sensory modalities.
Crossmodal correspondences are mediated by learned associations and shared semantic meanings or conceptual representations between sensory features.
Crossmodal correspondences develop through the statistical co-occurrence of features in the natural environment, leading to learned associations.
Crossmodal correspondences are driven by shared emotional or affective responses elicited by stimuli from different modalities.
Crossmodal correspondences are underpinned by overlapping neural representations or shared neural pathways in the brain.

A comprehensive understanding of crossmodal correspondences requires integrating multiple theoretical accounts (structural, semantic, statistical, emotional, neural) as they may operate at different levels or contribute to different types of correspondences.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper reviews and proposes multiple causal mechanisms by which unisensory features lead to consistent crossmodal associations.
